seo.title: Polar Circle Air-Cruise: Fly the Drake, Sail South
seo.description: Fly over the Drake Passage from Punta Arenas, then sail the Antarctic Peninsula south toward the Polar Circle on an 88-guest Magellan ship. Ten days, February only, from US$24,995 pp.

answer: The Polar Circle Air-Cruise is Antarctica21's ten-day, nine-night voyage from Punta Arenas, Chile. Guests fly about two hours to King George Island, then spend six days aboard Magellan Explorer or Magellan Discoverer, 88 guests at most, sailing the western Antarctic Peninsula and aiming far south toward the Polar Circle. It runs in February. Fares start from US$24,995 per person aboard Magellan Explorer and US$34,995 aboard Magellan Discoverer, double cabin.
quote: "I've stood on the Peninsula in March light. This is the voyage that goes past where I turned around."

suits: Two hours in the air instead of two days at sea, each way.
The Drake Passage is the roughest crossing on most Antarctic voyages. Flying it gives back four days and the seasickness that can come with them.
Antarctica21's longest air-cruise on the Peninsula.
Six days between the South Shetland Islands and the western Peninsula, and a push south toward the Polar Circle, ice and weather permitting.
Days among glaciers and icebergs on the western Peninsula. Wildlife is possible, never guaranteed.
Small enough that every guest can land at each stop within Antarctic visitor limits.

dayintro: The outline the ship sails south. Day order is indicative; the expedition team sets each day by weather and ice. Open a day for the detail.

days.title: Punta Arenas
days.body: Arrive in Punta Arenas, on the Strait of Magellan, and transfer to the hotel. Check in at Antarctica21's Explorers House before 2 PM for the mandatory briefing, then the welcome dinner.
days.stay: Cabo de Hornos Hotel or similar, Punta Arenas

days.title: Fly to King George Island
days.line: Over the Drake, not through it
days.body: A flight of about two hours carries you over the Drake Passage to King George Island in the South Shetlands. Guests walk past Chile's Frei Station and Russia's Bellingshausen Station to the shore, then board the ship by Zodiac. The flight goes only when the weather on the island allows; Antarctica21's contingency plan covers the wait in Punta Arenas.
days.stay: Aboard · Magellan Explorer or Magellan Discoverer
days.acts: Charter flight · Zodiac to the ship

days.title: The South Shetland Islands
days.body: The first full day in Antarctica, among the South Shetland Islands. The expedition team chooses the landings and Zodiac cruises on the day, by wind, swell and ice. Penguin colonies, fur and elephant seals and whalebone beaches are all possible here, never guaranteed.

days.title: The Gerlache Strait
days.body: Antarctica21 lists the Gerlache Strait as a possible route onto the western side of the Peninsula, with landings and Zodiac cruising chosen on the day.
days.acts: Landing · Zodiac cruise · kayaking (optional, priced separately)

days.title: The Penola Strait
days.body: Antarctica21 lists the Penola Strait as a possible route as the ship works south. Where the ship goes is set by ice and weather.

days.title: Crystal Sound, toward the Polar Circle
days.body: The aim is to sail far south toward the Polar Circle, through waters that may include Crystal Sound. How far the ship gets is decided on the day by ice and weather; Antarctica21 promises no crossing.

days.title: Northbound along the Peninsula
days.line: More landings on the way back
days.body: Northbound along the western Peninsula, with more landings and Zodiac outings.

days.title: Back to the South Shetlands
days.body: Back toward King George Island, with landings if conditions allow.

days.title: Fly to Punta Arenas
days.body: Fly from King George Island back to Punta Arenas, about two hours, weather permitting, and transfer to the hotel for the night. Meals in Punta Arenas that evening are at your own expense.
days.stay: Cabo de Hornos Hotel or similar, Punta Arenas

days.title: Departure
days.body: Breakfast at the hotel, then a group transfer to Punta Arenas airport. Patagonia is on the doorstep, and James can add it before or after the voyage.

exp_title: On the ice, on the water and ashore

experiences.name: South toward the Polar Circle
experiences.body: Antarctica21 aims far south toward the Polar Circle, through waters that may include Crystal Sound. Ice and weather decide how far the ship gets; no crossing is promised.

experiences.name: Zodiac cruises among the ice
experiences.body: Small boats among the icebergs, brash ice and glacier faces, with an expedition guide at the tiller. The way to see the ice up close, and the way ashore.
experiences.james: The bergs look big from the deck. From a Zodiac, they look like architecture.

experiences.name: Shore landings
experiences.body: Guided landings on the islands and the Peninsula, chosen on the morning by the expedition team. Penguin colonies and seals are possible at many landings, never guaranteed. Waterproof boots are lent on board.

experiences.name: Sea kayaking
experiences.body: Guided sea kayaking on selected departures, up to 20 paddlers in two alternating groups of 10, per Antarctica21. Places are limited, so it is booked with the voyage.
experiences.james: I paddled under the cliffs on the Peninsula in 2020. It was the quietest I've ever heard the world.

experiences.name: Hiking and snowshoeing
experiences.body: Small group hikes and snowshoe outings led by a guide, on selected departures.

experiences.name: Citizen science
experiences.body: Antarctica21 runs citizen science programmes on every expedition, with the expedition team.

vessel.title: The two ships, in detail
vessel.name: Magellan Explorer & Magellan Discoverer
vessel.blurb: Two small expedition ships built for Antarctic air-cruises, each carrying no more than 88 guests. The voyage is the same on either; the ship, the cabins and the fare are what change. Both are operated by Antarctica21.
facts: Launched 2019 · 90.7 m · LR PC6 ice class, built to Polar Code specifications · 88 guests on air-cruises · 60 staff and crew · seven cabin categories, all but the Porthole Cabin with outdoor seating
New for the 2026-27 season · 94 m · hybrid electric · PC6 ice class · 88 guests on air-cruises · 67 staff and crew · five cabin categories, all with private balconies
From US$24,995 pp (Explorer) · from US$34,995 pp (Discoverer) · double cabin
February, two departures each season; exact dates from Antarctica21

founder.title: Every Photograph Here Is His
founder.p1: James sailed the Antarctic Peninsula aboard HX's MS Roald Amundsen in February and March 2020, and was still there when the world shut down for COVID. Every photograph on this page outside the two Magellan ships is from that voyage: the Zodiacs among the bergs, the pink snow-algae landing, the kayaks under the cliffs, the postcard he wrote at Vernadsky Station.
founder.p2: He hasn't sailed this air-cruise or the two Magellan ships yet. It's on file for the travellers who ask him two things about Antarctica: can I skip the Drake, and can I go further south than the usual voyage?

firstTime.title: Why Fly In, and Why Go Farther South
firstTime.intro: Antarctica is a long way to go to spend four days of it crossing the Drake. This voyage spends them on the ice.
points: The Drake Passage takes about two days each way by sea. The flight takes about two hours.
Six days between the South Shetlands and the western Peninsula, aiming south toward the Polar Circle.
Two departures a season, per Antarctica21.
88 guests at most on an air-cruise.
Two hotel nights at the Cabo de Hornos Hotel or similar, transfers, the flights and the briefing are part of the fare. You only need to reach Punta Arenas.

faqs: Do you cross the Antarctic Circle?

Antarctica21 describes the goal as sailing far south toward the Polar Circle, via waters that may include the Gerlache and Penola straits and Crystal Sound. Ice and weather decide how far the ship gets.
Do I have to sail the Drake Passage?
No. You fly over it both ways, about two hours from Punta Arenas to King George Island.
Magellan Explorer and Magellan Discoverer, each with a maximum of 88 guests on air-cruises.
February. Antarctica21 announced two departures in each of the 2026-27 and 2027-28 seasons. Exact dates are not in the page text.
What happens if weather delays the flight?

Antarctica21 flies only when King George Island weather allows. Outbound, it keeps trying from Day 1 until 2 PM on Day 4, with Punta Arenas tours, meals and the Day 1 hotel covered while guests wait. If guests still cannot fly by then, the trip is cancelled and Antarctica21 refunds 100% of the cruise fare. On the way back, the ship keeps cruising until the flight is cleared, or guests fly up to a day early.
How much luggage can I take on the flight?

25 kg (55 lb) per person in total, hand luggage included, with no single item over 20 kg. Extra allowance cannot be bought. On the Classic and Polar Circle air-cruises, excess luggage is held in Punta Arenas until you return.

From US$24,995 per person, double cabin, aboard Magellan Explorer and from US$34,995 aboard Magellan Discoverer, as Antarctica21 shows them. The fare covers the flights, two nights at the Cabo de Hornos Hotel or similar in Punta Arenas, meals on board with wine and beer, landings, Zodiac cruises and lectures. Sea kayaking, hiking and snowshoeing are priced separately. Antarctica21 requires medical insurance with aero medical evacuation cover.
Dedicated single cabins carry no single supplement. In shared cabin categories Antarctica21 charges an 85% supplement on some cabins and 100% on the rest.
